exposure: day of primary wound repair since presentation
outcome: response after primary management in SSI
cohort: The study included 100 women who developed surgical site infection following a cesarean section.
finding: Factors such as socio-economic status, emergency/elective delivery, surgery timing (in labor or prelabor), personal hygiene, history of previous CS, anemia, wound grade, duration since membrane rupture, and timing of primary wound repair significantly affected wound healing after surgical site infection following cesarean section.
mod_finding: Emergency/elective delivery and the timing of surgery (during labor or prelabor) were identified as significant factors affecting wound healing after surgical site infection.
